vision.purpose:
A local-first pipeline of seven planning agents — CodeScanner, Brainstormer, Agentifier, Designer, StackAdvisor, Phaser, Deployer — that turns a rough idea or an existing codebase into a versioned folder of specs (`.spec4/v{N}/`), ready for a coding agent to execute phase by phase. Runs as a locally served web app at `localhost:8050`, with bring-your-own-key (BYOK) access across eight LLM providers; keys stay in the browser and never reach the server or disk.

This round's goal: finish the UI rework begun in v0 and continued in v1. The five screens left aside so far — directory picker, project-mode question, setup wizard, gate card, and Designer wizard — take the same dev-tool register already established for the app shell, home screen, chat frame, and Artifact View. The project view's element order also changes: agent rows (the controls) now come first, round cost second, round tree (the record) third. A new per-agent effort control is added alongside per-agent model selection. After this round, future_enhancements is empty — the register rollout is complete.
vision.ui_surface: Web app — Python, Dash, Dash Mantine Components — served locally at localhost:8050. Unchanged architecture; this round extends the existing dev-tool register to the five remaining screens, reorders the project view, and adds per-agent reasoning-effort selection — not a rewrite.
target_audience: Developers who already use Claude Code, Kiro, or similar AI coding agents daily, and who are skeptical of spec-driven tooling. Single audience — no secondary users.

Development Tool Shell.description: Header becomes a status bar: working directory (monospace), round (v{N}), default provider and model (monospace), Spec4 version. Primary nav: Project, Artifacts, Settings, plus one Docs link. Removes the external-link drawer, footer, and in-app landing page. Removes grid background, kicker labels, gradient text, hero spacing, card hover effects, button glows, and all emoji. Cuts vertical spacing roughly in half. Keeps the dark theme. #39FF14 green becomes the sole Mantine primary/accent color (primary buttons, active state, focus rings); secondary buttons are neutral outlines. #1E88E5 blue survives only in the wordmark. Monospace for any file, path, command, model name, or figure. When the status bar is too narrow for its slots, the working-directory path truncates first, from its start, so the project name at its tail stays readable; the round, provider, and model never truncate.
Development Tool Shell.example: The header reads as a status line, not a hero banner; under width pressure, only the path shortens, and only from the front.

Open To The Project.description: When a working directory is remembered, `/` opens the project view directly; otherwise it opens the directory picker. No introduction screen.
Open To The Project.example: Returning users land straight in their project, not on a splash page.

Round Tree.description: The project view's third element is the current round's `.spec4/v{N}/` folder as a tree: one line per artifact in pipeline order, each with a status — present, needs update (an upstream artifact is newer), or missing. Files are colored by lane with a three-item legend: prompts for the agent (phases/), reference for the agent (code_review.json, vision.json, feature_specs.json, ai_features.json, design/mock.html, design/manifest.json, stack.json), a record for you (deployment-plan.md, usage.json). Status comes from the existing dependency graph; usage.json is never marked needs-update. Each line opens the Artifact View at that file.
Round Tree.example: The round is shown as its files, now third in the project view's order.

Agent Rows.description: The seven agents as compact rows in pipeline order, now the project view's first element. Each row: agent name, the artifact it produces (monospace), the model it last ran on this round (from usage.json's per-agent models list; blank if it has not run), tokens in and out this round, and the action button using the existing state model — Start, Continue (an agent with an in-progress conversation and no artifact yet), Modify, Needs Update, Not Ready, Required — with its existing semantics and routing. No step numbers, descriptions, or emoji.
Agent Rows.example: A dense list of agent status rows, now the first thing the project view shows.

Round Cost.description: The round's estimated cost so far, from usage.json totals, now the project view's second element, following the existing labelling rules: labelled 'estimated', tokens shown, calls that could not be priced named and excluded, never '$0.0000' for unknown.
Round Cost.example: "Estimated cost, v0: $0.7312 · 2 of 19 calls could not be priced and are excluded" — never "$0.0000".

Artifact View.description: A screen at /artifacts that renders any file from the current round's .spec4/v{N}/ folder in monospace. Left: a round selector listing every round on disk (defaulting to the active round) above the round tree from the project view, same lanes and status flags, with the selected file marked. Right: the file — JSON pretty-printed, Markdown and other text as-is, with line numbers — under a one-line monospace header giving path, size, last modified, and lane. A Download button; for design/mock.html, also an 'Open rendered' button that opens the mock in a new tab the way the Designer wizard already does. A missing file shows its line in the tree and, when selected, the message 'missing — produced by {Agent}'. Only files in the reviewed artifact table are ever read, resolved strictly under the project's .spec4/ folder; no other path can be requested through this screen.
Artifact View.example: Selecting stack.json in the tree shows its path, size, and last-modified time above the pretty-printed JSON, with a Download button beside it.

Artifact Links.description: The Artifacts item is in the nav, between Project and Settings. Every line in the project view's round tree opens the Artifact View at that file. Every 'Download X' button in the chat frame's action row gains an 'Open X' button beside it that does the same.
Artifact Links.example: Clicking the vision.json line in the round tree opens the Artifact View with that file selected.

Chat Frame Register.description: The chat frame keeps every function it has — the agent pill bar, transcript, live progress bar with chars and elapsed counters, turn tokens, Fast Forward with its info modal, retry panel, breadth panel, downloads, continue buttons, composer, model chip, and status line — under the dev-tool register. Pill bar: the seven agents as plain text in pipeline order, the active one marked the way the active nav item is, completed ones at full weight, unreachable ones dimmed with the existing tooltip, no arrows between them; the pill bar's '← Back' button and every per-agent '← Back to X' button in the action row are removed, since the pill bar and the status bar's Project link already provide that navigation. Transcript: messages are blocks, not bubbles, with a dimmed one-word speaker label above each; the user's block carries a neutral left rule; no fills; default height grows to about 60% of the viewport, still scrollable. The run's cost, when a run completes, is shown as the same three-line strip the project view uses for round cost, replacing the prior card styling. Action row: counters (chars, turn tokens, elapsed) in monospace; one filled-green primary per row (the Continue button); Fast Forward, Download, Open, and Re-scan as neutral outlines (Re-scan in the warn tone); the 'Continue to Designer' skip beside 'Continue to Agentifier' stays an outline. Composer unchanged. Model chip shows the model name in monospace. Progress bar: thin, striped, animated — the only motion on screen, used purely as a live-activity signal.
Chat Frame Register.example: The pill bar reads as a row of plain labels, not a stepper with arrows; a completed run's cost shows as a plain three-line strip, not a card.

Entry Screens Register.description: The directory picker and the project-mode question take the register. Picker: the path input and every directory name in monospace; subdirectories as a single-column list, one per line, not a grid of buttons; the 'create a folder here' option folded into one row with its text field; Select is the one filled primary. Question: the title in sentence case, the explanation cut to two lines, the two choices as buttons on one row, one of them primary. Function unchanged: the picker still browses, creates, and selects; the question is still asked once per session.
Entry Screens Register.example: Subdirectories list as plain monospace lines, not a grid of tiles.

Setup Wizard Register.description: The three-step setup keeps its steps, fields, ids, and the shared provider/key/model fields it has in common with the gate. Each step's title becomes one short line and the explanatory paragraphs go. The three alerts go: 'your key is never stored outside your system' becomes one dimmed line under the key field; 'Connected to X' becomes one dimmed line above the model select; the Google free-tier warning is removed. The stepper stays, compact. Per step one filled primary (Connect, then Continue); Clear saved credentials a neutral outline in the warn tone; the within-wizard Back a neutral outline without the arrow glyph; the button that returns to the directory picker is removed — the status bar's path control does that. The model step also gains the effort select described under Per-Agent Effort. Success criteria: no button in the wizard returns to the directory picker.
Setup Wizard Register.example: The key field's helper text is one dimmed line, not an alert box.

Gate Card Register.description: The per-agent model gate — one component serving all seven agents in the chat frame and in front of the Designer wizard — becomes a panel: one line in monospace naming the agent and the default, e.g. 'Model for Brainstormer: claude-sonnet-5 · default', then the existing two- or three-button row: Use default is the filled primary; Pick a model and Keep <model> are neutral outlines. Expanding Pick swaps in the setup wizard's fields as today, so the two inherit together, including the effort select described under Per-Agent Effort. The 'Designer' title rendered above the gate on the Designer route goes — the status bar and pill bar already name the agent. Ids, callbacks, the single model-selection path, and the probe behaviour are untouched. Success criteria: the panel's first line names the agent and its default model in monospace.
Gate Card Register.example: "Model for Brainstormer: claude-sonnet-5 · default" followed by Use default / Pick a model / Keep <model>.

Designer Wizard Register.description: The wizard keeps its seven steps and stepper labels. The intro paragraph and the 'How to use Designer' accordion go. Each step carries at most one line of instruction above its controls. The screenshot and reference-image upload zones become 1px dashed outlines with one dimmed line of text. 'Mock approved and saved' becomes a dimmed line, not an alert, and so does the 'look and feel reference only' disclaimer above the preview. The stepper's circles and check icons go: it becomes a plain-text row like the chat frame's pill bar, the active step marked like the active nav item, completed steps at full weight, later steps dimmed. Per step one filled primary (Start, Next, Generate, Approve, Regenerate, Continue to StackAdvisor); Refine and Cancel neutral outlines; Start Over a neutral outline in the warn tone; the ↺ and → glyphs go. The preview iframe, fullscreen row, cost strip, and retry panel stay as they are. Success criteria: the stepper renders as a plain-text row with no circles or icons; the look-and-feel disclaimer and the 'approved and saved' notice each render as one dimmed line; each step has exactly one filled primary button.
Designer Wizard Register.example: The stepper reads Start · Sketch · Generate · Approve like the chat frame's pill bar, not a row of numbered circles.

Per-Agent Effort.description: The gate panel gains an Effort select beside the model, whose values are what the resolved model supports — always 'default', then low, medium, high, and xhigh or max only when the capability probe reports them; stored on the per-agent entry alongside the model. The setup wizard's model step gains the same control for the default, and an agent on 'default' inherits the default's effort as it inherits its model. Every LLM call passes it as LiteLLM's reasoning_effort with drop_params enabled, so an unsupported parameter is a silent no-op, never an error; 'default' at the setup level sends nothing. The status bar's model slot and the model chip show the effort after the model when it isn't default: 'claude-sonnet-5 · high'. usage.json records the effort per call. One resolution path: the gate, chip, retry panel and setup wizard read and write the same field through llm_selection.
Per-Agent Effort.example: "claude-sonnet-5 · high" in the model chip; "default" shows no suffix.

differentiators: The open `.spec4` file format — existing, unchanged; the round tree and Artifact View make it directly visible and navigable.
Any LLM model usable at any pipeline step — existing, unchanged.
constraints: Dash and Dash Mantine Components only — no new front-end dependency.
API keys never reach the server or disk.
The gate card, model chip, and retry panel share one model-selection path; nothing parallel is added.
Existing component ids are a test contract and are kept, except the Back buttons being removed, whose tests are updated.
usage.json stays out of the dependency graph (never contributes to staleness/status).
Standing rule for every element on screen: if it is not a fact, a command, an artifact, or a control, it goes.
Layout state lives in the two browser stores.
The accent is the theme primary color; no component sets a color locally.
Monospace for files, paths, model names, commands, and figures.
No decorative motion; motion is used only as a live-activity signal (e.g., the progress bar).
Artifact View reads only files in the reviewed artifact table, resolved strictly under the project's .spec4/ folder — no other path can be requested through this screen.
Reasoning effort is passed only through LiteLLM's reasoning_effort parameter with drop_params enabled; no provider-specific thinking parameters are constructed directly.

revision_history.goal: Extend the v0 dev-tool register to the chat frame and ship the Artifact View that the round tree was built to open into, completing the two v1 items scheduled in the previous round; the setup wizard, gate card, project-mode question, directory picker, and Designer wizard remain untouched (v2).
revision_history.rationale: These two features complete the v1 future-enhancement items scoped in the previous round: extending the dev-tool register to the chat frame, and building the Artifact View the round tree was designed to open into.

revision_history.goal: Finish the UI rework by extending the dev-tool register to the five remaining screens (directory picker, project-mode question, setup wizard, gate card, Designer wizard), reorder the project view so agent rows lead, and add explicit per-agent reasoning-effort selection alongside per-agent model selection. After this round, future_enhancements is empty.
revision_history.rationale: Completes the dev-tool register rollout across every remaining screen and reorders the project view so its controls (agent rows) lead over its record (round tree); corrects existing features' dependencies to their true prior-version relationships, ensuring nothing pre-existing depends on a feature added this round; and adds a single, LiteLLM-mediated per-agent effort control alongside the existing per-agent model control.
